keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1342-1343: Cliopatria's row begins in 1344, but the Zealots 'dominated political developments in Thessalonica from 1342 until 1350' and the Byzantine civil war page puts the uprising in 1342 (Kantakouzenos 'arrived too late to take the city' and marched out on 2 March 1342). The 1344 shape is used for the earlier years.

correction.text: shape unchanged; holds 1344-1350 (1351 is Byzantine again)

keyframe_review.note: Years only: 1,760 km2 (roughly a 24 km disc around Thessalonica) holds 1344-1350; Cliopatria's last year 1351 is after the Zealots' fall ('In 1350 Kantakouzenos ... made a triumphal entry into the city'). Neither page gives an area, and both treat only the city of Thessalonica ('the only Macedonian city that stayed in Byzantine hands' after the Serbian counteroffensive, civil-war page), so the hinterland disc is Cliopatria's convention, kept.

region.text: the city of Thessalonica and its hinterland

ledger.note: 1342: the Zealots take over Thessalonica. The Zealots 'dominated political developments in Thessalonica from 1342 until 1350'; Kantakouzenos's supporters under the governor Theodore Synadenos tried to hand the city to him, but 'The people of the city however reacted, ousted them and took control of the city' (Zealots page); 'an uprising led by a radical popular party, the Zealots' (civil-war page, which leads 'an autonomous regime unparalleled in Byzantine history'). No month is given. The 25 km radius is the researcher's reading of 'the city'.

1350: Kantakouzenos takes back Thessalonica. 'At the end of 1349, the people of the city finally rose in revolt against the Zealots, who were defeated'; Andreas Palaiologos fled to Mount Athos; 'In 1350 Kantakouzenos, accompanied by Emperor John Palaiologos and Palamas, made a triumphal entry into the city' (no month given). The civil-war page: 'Kantakouzenos recovered Thessalonica from the Zealots' while Dusan was occupied with Bosnia.
1350: the Zealots' commune ends with Kantakouzenos's entry into Thessalonica, the only Macedonian city still Byzantine after the Serbian conquests of 1345 onward (civil-war page).

wars.name: Byzantine civil war of 1341-1347 (Thessalonica)
wars.outcome: The Zealots hold Thessalonica against both the regency (Apokaukos and his son John) and Kantakouzenos, who 'camped outside the city' c. 1343 with Umur's fleet; 'a reinforced Thessalonica was able to hold out against a siege'. After Kantakouzenos wins the war (February 1347) 'the Zealots ignored the orders from Constantinople' and kept a 'de facto independent existence until Kantakouzenos conquered them in 1350'.
wars.note: Serres, loyal to the regency, fell to Dusan in September 1345; Thessalonica faced 'the continued threat of Stefan Dushan' (Zealots page).

wars.name: Kantakouzenos's reconquest of Thessalonica
wars.outcome: The city rises against the Zealots at the end of 1349; Kantakouzenos enters in 1350 with John V and Palamas.

certainty.note: Only the city of Thessalonica is named by the pages; its hinterland is Cliopatria's disc, not a documented boundary.

notes: Written 2026-10-19 by eu-05-e from two pages (budget 1-2). Cliopatria's row says 1344-1351 and cites the Wikipedia article 'Thessaloniki'; the pages say 1342-1350 and the state's own article is 'Zealots of Thessalonica' (identity.wikipedia and wikidata keep Cliopatria's values for the site's links). type is 'rebel': a civil-war regime that held a city against the regency and Kantakouzenos until crushed in 1350, though both pages also call it 'autonomous' and 'de facto independent'; neither calls it a commune or republic, so the Cliopatria name is kept as the display name. The Zealots 'throughout their existence ... continued to recognize the legitimate Emperor John V Palaiologos' (Zealots page). Not on the pages: months of the 1342 uprising and the 1350 entry; any territory beyond the city; the dates of Michael and Andreas Palaiologos's leadership (no rulers list is given). The pages differ on who governed (Michael Monomachos, Ioannes Batatzes and John Apokaukos in the Zealots page; John Apokaukos in 1342 in the civil-war page) and on how the 1345 killings fell; none moves a border. The byzantine-empire dossier has no 1342 loss or 1350 gain of Thessalonica yet and Cliopatria's Byzantine row may include the city in 1344-1351; the Byzantine group should subtract it for 1342-1350. Neither page gives an area, so no area comparison was possible.
